title: Junior Computational Geometry Engineer
description:
SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed. 

The Role As a Junior Computational Geometry Engineer, you work on the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack: the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model, reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right.
You start on well-scoped parts of that engine, next to the engineers who built it, and grow into owning them. Your code runs in the factory.

What We're Looking For - Foundations . Degree in computer science, mathematics, mechanical engineering or a related field, with real depth in geometry, linear algebra and numerics. Internships, thesis work or serious side projects count. We do not expect years of production experience.
- B-rep Basics . You are comfortable with topology, NURBS, meshes and point clouds. You may never have shipped a robust boolean, and you still understand why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations, and you want to learn how the field handles it.
- Kernel Exposure . You have worked with a geometry kernel and mesh libraries in at least one project: OpenCASCADE, CGAL, libigl, Open3D, PCL, Parasolid or comparable.
- Technical Ability . Solid modern C++ (17+) plus Python for tooling and rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write code others can read, test and maintain.
- Manufacturing Curiosity . You want to understand what happens once geometry meets a spindle, a nozzle or a fixture. CNC, additive or metrology exposure is a bonus, never a requirement.
- First Principles Thinker . You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you dig until you know whether the bug sits in the code, the model or the assumption.
- Learning Speed . You take direct feedback, apply it immediately, and close your own knowledge gaps without waiting to be taught.
- Industrial Grit . You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point.
- On - site . Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland.

What we're not looking for - Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship.
- CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them.
- Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll help define it.
- People who treat “it works on the test model” as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job.
- Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities.

What we offer - Mission : Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space.
- Total Ownership : High-stakes autonomy in your domain. You own both the problems and the solutions - and have the authority to execute.
- The Environment : Access to a 8,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial 3D printers. Your algorithms run on real hardware from day one.
- The Team : "Special Forces" model. Everyone senior, everyone ships. No politics, no bureaucracy. Direct feedback, high standards.
- Compensation : Competitive salary + meaningful equity.
- Location : Zurich HQ, with occasional time at Factory ONE in Munich.

Apply - Resume : Focus on the geometry work you have actually done. Thesis, internships, projects, coursework.
- GitHub / Portfolio : Show us the hardest problem you have solved. Code, a write-up, or a part that came off a machine because of you.
- Cover letter : Why this mission? Why now? What would you build first?

title: Internship position for World Models for Software Architecture (Constructor Fabric)
description:
About the Project 

Constructor Fabric turns a company's informal knowledge into production software through a pipeline of composable capability units called gears : requirements → architecture → product fit → framework (G1) → application → runtime. We are building a World Model over that pipeline — a model that does not just generate code, but predicts the consequences of an architectural decision: total cost of ownership, unintended side effects, latency and failure behaviour, and whether a proposed composition is even admissible.
The central object is not a digital twin of the application but its formal architectural skeleton : gear contracts (GearSpec), a typed attributed hypergraph of the application (AppGraph), a composition algebra that defines which assemblies are legal, and several semantic projections (types, protocols, resources, security) over which properties are proved, refuted by counterexample, or reported as an explainable gap . All of it is written in a domain-specific language whose syntax trees and graphs we keep in a projectional editor (JetBrains MPS) — so the DSL is not a convenience layer, it is the thing that defines the model's state space and the boundary of what the model is allowed to propose.

Internship Role 

As a Research Intern (Machine Learning for Software Engineering), you will support the data and modelling work behind the World Model — mining code, building datasets, and running baseline experiments. We are looking for students who are keen to collaborate with industrial companies working with AI, open to out-of-the-box topics, and interested in a long-term collaboration.

Key Responsibilities 

- Mine open-source repositories and extract architecture, dependency, and interface graphs from code.

- Help build and clean (specification → architecture) datasets, including synthetic project generation.

- Implement and evaluate baseline models (heuristic search, graph ML, or LLM generation) for single pipeline steps.

- Benchmark models against shared datasets and metrics to compare approaches.

- Build evaluation harnesses and track experiments reproducibly.

- Assist with documentation and, where relevant, publication activities.

Required Qualifications 

- Currently enrolled in a BSc/MSc in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, or similar.

- Experience with Python and ML frameworks (PyTorch, scikit-learn).

- Interest in machine learning for code, software engineering, or formal methods.

- Good English and teamwork skills.

Desired Qualifications 

- Predictive models/time-series/etc.

- LLM tooling.

- Familiarity with graph machine learning (PyTorch Geometric or DGL).

- Interest in formal methods, program or static analysis, or working with code structure (e.g. AST manipulation, tree-sitter, or repository mining).

Application Details 

Please submit:

- CV

- Short motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining your interest and relevant skills

- Transcript of records (GPA obligatory)

Wat ga je doen?

Als test engineer ben je verantwoordelijk voor de verwerking, validatie en presentatie van windtunneldata aan de klant. Je werkt daarbij vanaf de start van een project tot en met de aflevering van windtunnel testresultaten nauw samen met klanten en collega’s. Bij de voorbereiding en uitvoering van de test weet jij de diverse meetgegevens en data te verifiëren, verwerken en presenteren aan onze klanten, zodat zij deze vlot kunnen interpreteren. Je werkt hiervoor samen met technici operators en projectmanagers. Je ontwikkelt multidisciplinaire kennis en doet ervaring op met het volledige proces, van data-acquisitie en geavanceerde meettechnieken tot de uiteindelijke verwerking en analyse van de data. Kortom een uitdagende baan waarbij er ruimte is voor eigen inbreng en je veel verantwoordelijkheid krijgt. Je werkt primair op onze locatie in Marknesse, waar wij twee lage snelheidswindtunnels beheren. Op projectbasis ondersteun je ook onze windtunneltesten in Amsterdam.

Wat breng je mee?

• Een brede technische opleiding (HBO) met kennis en ervaring op vlak van aerodynamica, instrumentatie en dataverwerking

Wat bieden wij jou?

Werken bij NLR, betekent werken in een nationale en internationale hightech omgeving. Samenwerken en betrokkenheid staan bij ons hoog in vaandel. De Duits-Nederlands Windtunnels (DNW) exploiteert windtunnels op vier verschillende locaties van het Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum (NLR) en van de Duitse zusterorganisatie DLR. In deze zeer geavanceerde installaties wordt hoog gekwalificeerd onderzoek verricht voor internationale opdrachtgevers, voornamelijk uit de luchtvaart en automotive sector. Acquisitie wordt niet op prijs gesteld!

title: Brand Data Production Manager (m/f/d)
description:
At Statista , we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

Your role 

As Brand Data Production Manager, you are the driving force behind Statista’s brand-related data portfolio. You own the brand data Type as a data product, with decision-making authority over what brand data to produce, develop, maintain, or retire, set priorities and quality bar that guide the teams who build and run the data pipelines.

- Own the end-to-end lifecycle of brand data domains- including brand market shares, consumer awareness, brand perception, and loyalty metrics- defining the strategic direction, target users, and value proposition and serving as the central point of contact for what brand data should cover and why.

- Translate market trends, customer needs and use cases into clear coverage priorities and requirements, turning signals from Revenue, Quality, platform and API usage, customer feedback, and industry developments into a prioritized brand data roadmap.

- Identify data coverage gaps and define pragmatic solutions evaluating potential data sources, proxy data strategies, and methodology trade-offs to close critical gaps, weighing relevance against feasibility in collaboration with production teams.

- Define and track business-facing KPIs such as coverage of priority brands, data quality, and customer impact; establish and maintain quality gates, data governance standards, and escalation processes across the production pipeline, working with the Quality team to drive continuous improvement.

- Review and challenge trade-offs proposed by production and engineering teams (e.g. coverage vs. speed, automation vs. accuracy) from a relevance and customer-value perspective, while production line owners retain responsibility for how data is produced.

- Coordinate cross-functionally with Data Engineering, Content, Product, and commercial stakeholders to resolve dependencies and keep priorities aligned across the organization.

Your Profile 

- Strong background in data product management, data operations, market/brand strategy, or business analytics, with the judgment to decide what data matters most and why and a track record of owning and driving a data domain or product area. Degree in a related field and/or equivalent practical experience.

- Solid understanding of data concepts and statistical reasoning, paired with a strong customer-focused business mindset and an understanding of how data creates value for users.

- Comfortable setting direction while depending on others for execution; you lead through clarity, prioritization, and evidence rather than direct control of delivery.

- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills, experienced in translating complex business needs into actionable specifications for technical teams and briefing production teams around clear, well-justified priorities. Clear, confident communicator in English who excels at data storytelling and explains complex topics clearly.

- A structured, pragmatic, and curious way of working, with an ownership mindset and the ability to stay calm and decisive under pressure.

- Proficiency in Excel required; SQL and BI tools (Power BI, Tableau, Looker) and project tools (Jira, Confluence) are a plus. Experience with market research or API-sourced data, Python, or cloud data platforms is an additional advantage.

What we offer 

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

- Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

- Hybrid work and flex-time

- International team and social events

- Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

- Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

- Career & training opportunities

- Attractive locations and modern offices

- Mental health support with OpenUp

Some of the benefits listed here apply only to the German entity and to Junior-level roles or above.

title: Head of Investment Fund Operations
description:
We are seeking a highly experienced Head of Fund Operations to oversee the operational management of a diverse Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio within an established international private banking environment.

In this responsible leadership role, you will manage a small team of fund operations specialists and ensure reliable, accurate and efficient processes across fund data, cost management, NAV controls and reporting. You will work closely with internal stakeholders as well as fund administrators, system providers, auditors, tax advisors and other external partners. As a member of the Valuation Committee, you will also contribute your expertise to fund valuation-related decisions.

The position offers a combination of team leadership, fund operations expertise, data management, regulatory knowledge and process automation , with considerable scope to improve existing processes and further professionalise the operational setup.

Location: Basel

Your Responsibilities: 

- Manage and develop a team of three Fund Operations specialists and oversee operations for the complete Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio

- Ensure the availability, integrity and quality of fund data across the relevant internal systems

- Monitor end-to-end data flows and act as the key contact for the external system provider

- Review and validate important fund indicators such as TER, PTR, OGC and transaction costs

- Take ownership of the PRIIPs KID production process and ensure that the underlying information is accurate and up to date

- Manage the relationship with CACEIS concerning NAV data, including plausibility controls and the investigation and resolution of discrepancies

- Participate in valuation-related decisions as an active member of the Valuation Committee

- Coordinate the preparation and publication of annual and semi-annual fund reports

- Liaise with auditors and tax advisors and oversee relevant fund-related tax topics

- Review fund-related invoices and ensure transparency and accuracy of associated costs

- Coordinate the preparation of factsheets, monthly fund manager reports and regular reporting for wholesale clients

- Analyse existing processes and identify opportunities for greater efficiency, automation and data quality

- Drive the use of automation and data-driven approaches to improve fund operations and reporting

- Ensure that operational processes and reporting activities are aligned with applicable Swiss and Luxembourg regulatory requirements

- Serve as a knowledgeable and reliable contact for internal stakeholders and external service providers across fund operations

Your Profile: 

- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in fund operations, fund controlling, fund accounting, fund administration or fund audit

- Comprehensive knowledge of the Swiss and Luxembourg fund landscape, ideally including CISA, FINMA, AMAS, UCITS and CSSF regulations

- Practical experience with NAV control and oversight and cooperation with external fund administrators

- Previous experience with CACEIS is considered an advantage

- Strong knowledge of fund reporting, data management, valuation processes and fund-related cost structures

- Good technical capabilities, including Python or a comparable scripting language, advanced Excel and experience working with databases and SQL

- Experience in automating operational, data or reporting processes is highly desirable

- Strong analytical skills and a precise, structured approach to complex data and processes

- A proactive, hands-on working style with a high degree of personal responsibility

- Previous leadership or people management experience is an advantage

- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across different functions and organisations

- High level of integrity, reliability and accountability

- Comfortable working in an international, regulated financial services environment

- University or FH degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Accounting or a comparable discipline

- Excellent English skills; German and French are advantageous

What We Offer: 

- A senior position with broad responsibility for the operational management of a Swiss and Luxembourg fund portfolio

- The opportunity to shape and further improve the Fund Operations function and its processes

- A varied role combining leadership, fund operations, data and automation

- Regular interaction with senior internal stakeholders and key external partners

- The opportunity to contribute to the Valuation Committee and support important fund-related decisions

- Significant scope to introduce process improvements and strengthen automation and data quality

- An international environment within an established and reputable private banking organisation

- Flexible working arrangements and a modern working environment

- Opportunities for continued professional and personal development

title: Product Owner Cloud Competence Center
Data Scientist
Expert Financial Performance & Value Creation (m/w/d)
description:
Die Chance

Steuerberatungen rechnen rückwärts. Sie wissen genau, was im letzten Jahr passiert ist, und erstaunlich wenig darüber, welches Mandat, welche Leistung und welcher Mitarbeiter morgen Geld verdient.

Vogel erwirbt eigenständige Beratungsunternehmen und baut sie zur stärksten Adresse ihrer Region aus. Mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen vertrauen uns ihre steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Themen an. Wir wachsen aus dem Bestand und durch Übernahmen. Beides stellt dieselbe Frage in zwei Formen: Was verdienen unsere Mandate, Leistungen und Teams tatsächlich, und was folgt daraus für die nächsten zwölf Monate.

Die Rolle ist auf ein bis drei Jahre Beratungserfahrung zugeschnitten. Du treibst die finanzielle Steuerung von der Ertragsseite her. Du siehst auf die Zahlen, erkennst, wo Ertrag liegen bleibt, und gehst damit zu den Menschen, die es ändern können, auch wenn das Gespräch unangenehm wird. So lange, bis die Wirkung in den Zahlen steht. Du berichtest an Moritz Bonacker.

Was du verantwortest

Ertragskraft und Produktivität

- Durchleuchte die Bestände auf den echten Daten des laufenden Rechnungswesens, von der Mandatsgröße bis zum Deckungsbeitrag, und mach sichtbar, was heute stillschweigend miterbracht und nicht abgerechnet wird.

- Bewerte die Produktivität auf beiden Seiten: je Leistungsart, welche ihren Deckungsbeitrag trägt und welche quersubventioniert wird, und je Mitarbeiter, wo Wertschöpfung je eingesetzter Stunde entsteht.

- Dein Maßstab: keine Analyse ohne benannte Maßnahme, benannten Verantwortlichen und benanntes Datum.

Durchsetzung

- Führ die Honorargespräche selbst oder mit einem Berufsträger an deiner Seite. Und sprich auch die unangenehmen Fälle aus: Nicht jedes Mandat hat einen Weg in die Profitabilität.

- Geh mit deinen Zahlen direkt zu den fachlich Verantwortlichen: was ihre Mandate und Teams produzieren, wo Ertrag liegen bleibt, was sich konkret ändern muss.

- Verfolge die Maßnahmen nach, bis das Ergebnis in den Zahlen steht. Auch wenn es unbequem wird.

Zukauf und Vorausschau

- Entwickle je Übernahme den Wertsteigerungsplan auf der finanziellen Seite und verfolge ihn über Jahre statt über hundert Tage. Dein Maßstab: Die dritte Übernahme läuft besser als die erste, weil du beide gemacht hast.

- Verantworte Umsatz- und Ergebnisprognose, Budgets, Szenarien und Abweichungsanalysen über alle Standorte, auch die neu dazugekommenen.

- Automatisiere, was du baust. Keine Auswertung, die jemand monatlich manuell zusammensetzt.

Fragen, auf die du die Antwort findest

- Ein Mandat trägt seinen Deckungsbeitrag nicht, die Beziehung besteht seit fünfzehn Jahren: Wie gehst du in dieses Gespräch, und wo ist deine Grenze?

- Woran unterscheidest du eine Leistung, die zu billig ist, von einer, die zu aufwendig erbracht wird?

- Deine Empfehlung wird von jemandem blockiert, der dir nicht berichtet. Was tust du, wenn das zweite Gespräch auch nichts bringt?

Woran wir Erfolg messen

- Nach 6 Monaten: Der erste Bestand ist vollständig durchgerechnet, Deckungsbeitrag je Mandat und Leistungsart liegen belastbar vor, die erste Auswertung läuft automatisiert, die ersten Honorargespräche hast du selbst geführt.

- Nach 12 Monaten: Die erste Anpassungswelle ist über den Bestand gefahren, das erreichte Honorarniveau nachgewiesen. Die Deckungsbeitragsrechnung wird in Führungsentscheidungen verwendet. Deine Prognose trägt, ihre Abweichung kannst du erklären.

- Nach 24 Monaten: Mehrere Übernahmen begleitet, die spätere lief nachweislich besser als die erste. Die Steuerung läuft weitgehend automatisiert, dein Anteil hat sich von der Aufbereitung zur Interpretation verschoben.

- Wohin es führt: in die Senior-Stufe der fachlichen Expertenlaufbahn, mit größerem Themenfeld und mehr methodischer Autorität. Willst du ein Team aufbauen, steht dir die Führungslaufbahn ebenso offen. Entschieden am Beitrag und nicht am Berufsjahr.

Was du mitbringst

- Du hast ein bis drei Jahre in der Beratung gearbeitet, in der Strategieberatung, in Transaction Services oder in einem Wertsteigerungs-Team: kommerzielle Prüfung, Pricing, Ergebnisverbesserung.

- Du hast Profitabilität auf Kunden-, Produkt- oder Leistungsebene gerechnet und die Ergebnisse gegenüber Entscheidern vertreten, nicht nur aufbereitet.

- Du führst unangenehme Gespräche, statt sie aufzuschieben, ob es um Geld oder um Leistung geht, und hältst deine Position, wenn Widerspruch kommt.

- Du beherrschst Excel jenseits von Pivot-Tabellen und liest eine Buchführung, ohne Steuerberater zu sein. SQL oder Python sind kein Zusatz, sondern der Weg, dieselbe Auswertung nicht zweimal von Hand zu bauen.

- Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Datenanalyse, Mustererkennung in Bestandsdaten und Drafting.

- Du bewegst Menschen ohne Weisungsbefugnis, über eine Rechnung, die niemand bestreiten kann, und über einen Ton, der Widerstand nicht erzeugt. Und du setzt in allem den höchsten Standard, weil Mittelmaß für dich keine Option ist.

Ein Plus, keine Bedingung

- Erfahrung aus einem Wertsteigerungsprogramm nach einer Übernahme. Dass du es nie selbst zu Ende umgesetzt hast, ist kein Ausschluss, genau das ist hier die Aufgabe.

- Nähe zur Steuerberatung oder zu einer anderen Dienstleistung, die in Stunden verkauft wird.

- Kein kanonischer Lebenslauf nötig: Steuerberater mit ausgeprägter Zahlen- und Preisneigung, Bank- oder Beteiligungsprofil mit Wunsch nach einer operativen Rolle, Praxismanager, der eine Einheit nachweislich auf Deckungsbeitrag umgestellt hat. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala: Das obere Ende steht für den Umfang des verantworteten Themenfelds und für die Fähigkeit, Menschen ohne Weisungsbefugnis zu bewegen. Ein anderer Hintergrund startet zu einem anderen Marktpreis und konvergiert nach zwölf Monaten bewährter Leistung auf das Rollen-Niveau.

Was diese Rolle ist, und was nicht

- Rechnen und sprechen, nicht abgeben. Du gibst das Ergebnis nicht ab, du führst das Gespräch darüber. Wäre das eine Excel-Rolle, wäre sie falsch geschnitten.

- Entscheidungen tragen, nicht dokumentieren. Jede Zahl, die du baust, muss eine Entscheidung tragen. Monatsabschluss-Kommentierung ohne Konsequenz gibt es hier nicht.

- Überzeugen, nicht anweisen. Die Berufsträger und Teams, mit denen du arbeitest, berichten nicht an dich. Wer Widerstand über Hierarchie löst, kommt hier nicht weit.

Warum Vogel

- Die Frage ist im Markt ungelöst. Kaum ein Haus dieser Branche kennt seinen Deckungsbeitrag je Mandat. Du baust die Antwort.

- Du siehst, was aus deiner Empfehlung wird. Hier begleitest du dieselben Mandate über Jahre, statt nach der Abgabe zu gehen.

- Du willst entscheiden: Methode, Kennzahlen und Reihenfolge. Kein Gremium überstimmt dich. Vogel ist hierarchisch in der Entscheidung, flach in der Kommunikation, autonom in der Ausführung. Leistung wird gefeiert, nicht versteckt.

- Substanz im Rücken. Ein profitables, wachsendes Unternehmen mit etablierten Mandanten. Was du verbesserst, wirkt auf eine Basis, die bereits trägt.

FAQ 

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr? 

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen? 

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet? 

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung? 

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung? 

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es? 

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub? 

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. title: Senior Computational Geometry Engineer
description:
SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed.

The Role As a Computational Geometry Engineer, you own the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack - the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model and reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right.
You own the code that runs in the factory.

What We're Looking For - 5+ years building geometry-heavy software in production - CAD/CAM, geometry kernels, feature recognition, CAE/simulation preparation, metrology, or comparable.
- B-rep and Mesh Depth . You think natively in topology and NURBS. Feature recognition, defeaturing, robust booleans, offsetting, surface/surface intersection, healing and repair. You know exactly why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations - and what to do about it. You have had the opportunity to delve into complex CAD models and are able to assess their quality in both quantitative and qualitative terms (gaps in edge, spikes in loops, tiny elements, twisted surfaces...) and ultimately predict which types of processing might be challenged.
- Kernel Fluency . Hands-on with a geometry kernel - Parasolid, OpenCASCADE, ACIS, or equivalent - and the judgment to know which parts can be developed in-house in order to retain full control and IP rights, and which parts too complex (e.g. advanced solvers) should be integrated as 3rd parties. Comfortable with mesh and point-cloud processing (libigl, Open3D, CGAL, PCL) alongside solid modelling.You know well STEP file format and about integration into collaboration & interoperability processes.
- Technical Excellence . Strong command of modern C++ (17+), plus Python for rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write and test performant code. 
- Manufacturing Instinct . Some knowledge of fabrication techniques-casting, stamping, composites, and additive manufacturing-alongside toolsets for evaluating design manufacturability, risk profiles, quality standards, and cost factors.
- End-to-End Ownership . Algorithm design through to a shipped, tested, maintained service.
- First Principles Thinker. You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you know whether the bug is in the code, the model, or the assumption.
- Industrial Grit . You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point.
- Maniacal Urgency . Speed is our only edge. You thrive in the "chaos-to-order" phase of a startup.
- On-site : Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland.

What we're not looking for - Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship.
- CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them.
- Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll go find it.
- People who treat "it works on the test model" as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job.
- Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities.

What we offer - Mission : Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space.
- Total Ownership : High-stakes autonomy in your domain. You own both the problems and the solutions - and have the authority to execute.
- The Environ ment : Access to a 8,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial 3D printers. Your algorithms run on real hardware from day one.
- The Tea m : "Special Forces" model. Everyone senior, everyone ships. No politics, no bureaucracy. Direct feedback, high standards.
- Compensation : Competitive salary + meaningful equity.
- Location : Zurich HQ, with occasional time at Factory ONE in Munich.

Apply Resume : Focus on geometry systems you've built and owned.
GitHub/Portfolio : Show us the hard problem you solved - code, papers, or parts that came off a machine because of you.
Cover letter : Why this mission? Why now? What would you build first?

title: Software Engineer, AI Enablement
description:
Thank you for considering Tailscale . If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic! 

About Tailscale 

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role 

We're seeking a talented and motivated full-time Software Engineer, AI Enablement to help Tailscale's engineering organization get the most out of AI-assisted development. You'll join a small, high-leverage team reporting to our co-founder, working alongside our first AI enablement engineer to build the tools, workflows, and practices that help every engineer at Tailscale build faster and more safely with AI. This is a foundational role — you'll have real latitude to shape what AI enablement means here as we scale, with direct visibility into how the whole engineering org adopts these tools.

Key Responsibilities 

- Partner with engineering leadership and Tailscale's technical staff to define and drive our internal AI-enablement roadmap.

- Work closely with the team building Aperture by Tailscale, our AI gateway used both internally and offered as a product.

- Build and iterate on the tools, workflows, and shared practices that help engineers get real value from coding agents — and evaluate new models and tools, making clear calls on what we adopt.

- Partner with engineering and non-engineering teams to find high-leverage opportunities to apply AI — this is a support function, so success means other teams shipping faster because of what you've built.

- Establish the guardrails, review practices, and documentation that make AI-generated code safe to ship, and act as the internal advocate who helps teams adopt good practices without mandating a single tool.

- Track adoption and measure the real impact of AI tooling on velocity and quality, and report back to leadership.

What We Are Looking For 

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience

- Genuine, daily, hands-on fluency with modern AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, or similar) — real power-user experience, not occasional use

- Experience building and shipping internal tools or developer-facing automation

- Strong written and verbal communication and internal advocacy skills — comfortable teaching, writing, and influencing engineers at very different comfort levels with AI tooling

- A balanced approach — trying to get people to use AI effectively and safely where appropriate. We don't have an 'AI mandate'; we believe that if we make AI both easy to use and safe, people will choose to use it when appropriate.

- Comfort with ambiguity and self-directed prioritization on a small, still-forming team

- Product or systems thinking — able to identify and prioritize high-leverage opportunities, not just execute a pre-set roadmap

Nice to Have

- Prior experience in developer experience, platform engineering, or internal tooling

- Experience evaluating or benchmarking LLMs and coding agents

- Experience with a systems language such as Go or Rust, in addition to Python

- Background in security or code-review practices — helpful for reasoning about AI/agent-generated code, though you don't need to be a security engineer

- Experience in developer relations, technical evangelism, or customer-facing developer advocacy — the same skills that make someone effective in external DevRel translate well to driving internal AI adoption

- Technical project management experience

As a company, we strive to maintain fair and equitable compensation practices within our team across all roles and all levels. Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.

UK Pay Range

£128,770—£178,540 GBP

What We Offer 

- An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.

- A competitive total compensation package. This includes a base salary, an equity incentive plan and variable commission (for quota-based roles).

- Comprehensive group benefits with no waiting period. Take advantage of coverage for health, vision, dental, and more for you and your family!

- Remote first company —most of our teams work fully remotely. Enjoy a change of scenery wherever you can get wifi, participate in virtual and in-person social events, and leverage our corporate co-working program to visit WeWork (or other similar spaces near you). Some roles require in-office collaboration depending on team needs, which will be clearly noted in the job description.

- Employer-funded retirement contributions. Tailscale will match your retirement contributions dollar-for-dollar, up to a maximum annual employer contribution equal to 0.75% of your eligible compensation.

- Connect with other Tailscalars IRL. Attend our annual company retreat, participate in team off-sites, and collaborate in person with teammates across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Singapore. We support intentional in-person connection through team travel and distributed collaboration. 

- Support for your personal and professional development. Grow your career thoughtfully with $1500 USD annually for professional development, or take advantage of mentorship, coaching, and internal promotion opportunities. 

- Paid time off and a healthy work-life integration. Our flexible, paid time off program supports you for any situation life throws your way, whether moving homes or travelling the world! 

- A build-your-own home office setup. You choose your own company-owned laptop (Mac or PC), receive a monthly home internet reimbursement, and $500 USD to customize your workstation to make it your own. 

- Paid parental leave program . We care about your life outside of work and encourage new parents to take advantage of parental leave top-ups (20 weeks for birthing parents, 16 weeks for non-birthing parents).

Tailscale is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring process. If you require an accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process or related to any aspect of this role, please contact your recruiter. 

Our hiring process uses AI-assisted tools to help screen and assess candidates. All hiring decisions are made by people. 

Please be aware that legitimate emails from Tailscale's talent team will only originate from @tailscale.com, @greenhouse.io, and @interviews.modernloop.io email addresses. For more information about protecting yourself from impersonators and scams, please visit https://tailscale.com/scam-awareness .

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Join our mission 

We're proud to work with many incredible companies, accelerating their ability to build their products. 

We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.

After experiencing this pain firsthand at companies of every size, we set out to build the developer infrastructure platform we'd always wanted to use. Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.

Today, we're already accelerating hundreds of companies around the world, helping them ship features instead of waiting for infrastructure. We've built something that feels almost magical in its simplicity: change your runs-on line, mount your toolchain cache directory and suddenly your builds are 5x faster.

About the role 

Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.

As a DevOps Engineer at Namespace, you'll build and operate the infrastructure that makes this performance possible. You'll own the compute, storage, and networking behind every build our customers run, keeping the platform fast, reliable, and cost-effective as we accelerate more companies around the world.

Our culture 

We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. If you care about building, moving fast, and making real impact, you'll fit right in.

What you'll do 

- Own the reliability, performance, and scalability of the infrastructure that runs every customer’s build, test, and CI job on Namespace.

- Optimize performance across compute, memory, storage, and networking.

- Automate provisioning, deployment, scaling, and recovery across our fleet.

- Build observability, alerting, and incident response processes that identify and resolve issues before they affect customers.

- Drive capacity planning and cost efficiency, so we continue to deliver infrastructure that is both faster and more cost-effective.

- Collaborate closely with product engineers to ship new capabilities quickly and safely.

What we're looking for 

- Strong engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience operating production infrastructure at scale.

- Deep knowledge of Linux, networking, and storage, plus experience with tools like Kubernetes, Terraform, or similar.

- Proficiency in Go, Python, or a similar language, automation is paramount.

- Deep experience with observability tooling and participating in on-call rotations.

- A strong focus on performance and a rigorous approach to measuring and improving it.

- Bonus: experience with bare metal, virtualization (KVM, Firecracker), or running CI/CD systems at scale.

You can expect: 

- Competitive salary and stock options

- Flexible working hours

- Market-leading parental leave

Life at Namespace Labs: 

- We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.

- We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.

- We believe in being fully transparent internally on how decisions are made, on how the company is doing, and we use that information to drive our decisions.

title: Full Stack Web Engineer
description:
Location: Remote – Latin America (Open to applicants located anywhere in the LATAM region)

Fueled is a leading digital strategy, design, and engineering agency. We are a 300+ person team that has designed and built hundreds of digital products and experiences for brands like Google, Apple, The New York Times, ESPN, Victoria's Secret, MGM Resorts, Albertsons, and CLEAR.

As a Full Stack Web Engineer at Fueled, your mission is to turn well-defined tickets and user stories into clean, production-ready code that powers large-scale digital experiences. Working within enterprise WordPress engagements, you'll build and deliver features end-to-end, from the frontend experience to modern PHP, JavaScript, and Gutenberg blocks in React.js. You'll bring designs and requirements to life within themes and plugins, moving quickly and confidently by pairing your own craft with AI-assisted workflows, thorough documentation, and the support of senior engineers who review and elevate your work.

This is a role for engineers who love the craft: you write code you're proud of, you welcome sharp code review, and you treat AI tools as a force multiplier, not a substitute for understanding. You should be comfortable taking a feature from requirements through implementation, making sound decisions along the way, and delivering a polished, production-ready result. Your work will ship to platforms serving millions of visitors, alongside a team recognized as one of the top enterprise WordPress practices in the world.

Intentionally remote, our team thrives in a culture that values flexibility, creativity, and cutting-edge technology. For engineers in Latin America, that means real-time collaboration with US-based teams during your normal working day, compensation in USD, and a seat at the table on projects for globally recognized brands – all from wherever you work best. Together, we're shaping the future of digital experiences.

What you will do:

- Build features for enterprise-level WordPress solutions – custom Gutenberg blocks in React.js, plugins, and themes using modern HTML/CSS and well-structured PHP.

- Own tickets end-to-end: understand the requirements, make sound decisions when details are incomplete, and deliver reviewable pull requests with clear summaries of your approach, assumptions, and testing.

- Bring designs and user experiences to life by translating Figma designs and other project requirements into polished, responsive features and reusable components within WordPress themes and plugins.

- Leverage AI tools as a core part of your daily workflow to accelerate implementation and debugging while critically validating every output before it reaches a pull request.

- Iterate on code review feedback from senior and lead engineers, absorbing patterns and best practices that sharpen your craft with every merge.

- Collaborate proactively and asynchronously in English with distributed teammates across engineering, design, and delivery.

What you will achieve:

- Within your first month, you'll have shipped merged, production-ready pull requests on a live client project, demonstrating that you can take written direction and run with it.

- By the 3-month mark, you'll be independently owning tickets from requirement to release, with review cycles getting shorter as your grasp of our conventions deepens.

- Your AI-assisted workflow will have measurably accelerated delivery on your project – without ever compromising the quality bar our clients expect.

- You'll have earned the trust of your engineering leads as a dependable contributor whose PRs are a pleasure to review.

- By the end of your contract, you'll have a portfolio of enterprise-grade work, sharpened skills, and a standing invitation for future collaboration.

About you:

- You have solid agency or consultancy experience building WordPress solutions for large-scale, enterprise projects – high-traffic sites, demanding clients, real deadlines.

- You're comfortable working across the web stack, including HTML, CSS, modern PHP, JavaScript, and the Gutenberg ecosystem, including building custom blocks with React.js. Bonus points if you've worked with our open-source tools, like ElasticPress or ClassifAI – tell us about it in your application.

- AI tools are already part of how you work: you use them to move faster, and you know exactly when they're wrong.

- You're passionate about sharpening your craft – you read best practices for fun, seek out code review, and never ship code you don't understand.

- You communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken, and can confidently walk a reviewer through your decisions, assumptions, and tradeoffs.

- You're based in Latin America, and thrive on a distributed team, collaborating in real time with US time zones from the remote location of your choice.

Contractor Fee

Compensation is determined based on a variety of factors including relevant experience, projects, geographic location, and business needs. Contractor fees are paid in USD.

Join our Contractor Pool 

This role is designed as a contract position, offering you the opportunity to experience our team and culture while showcasing your contributions. When the fit and business needs align, some contractors are invited to explore a transition into full-time roles.

If you are passionate about Fueled's mission and think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, even if you don't check all the boxes – please apply. We'd appreciate the opportunity to review your application. Everyone gets a response.

Upon meeting the necessary criteria, you'll join the Fueled contractor network, granting you access to project invitations tailored to your expertise and availability when they arise.

Any data provided will be processed in accordance with applicable law and our privacy policy . Curious about what to expect during our talent process? Check it out here .

Loft Orbital | Senior Cloud Infrastructure Engineer (SRE) | Golden, CO or San Francisco, CA | $180k–$240k + equity | https://loftorbital.com Loft builds and operates shareable satellites so customers can fly a payload without building a spacecraft. We integrate, launch, and operate the mission end to end: Earth observation, IoT, on-orbit AI, national security. 30+ missions flown since 2017, fleet on track for 30 satellites by 2027, offices in SF, Golden, and Toulouse. Our Cloud Infrastructure team runs the ground segment that talks to the fleet. This is an SRE role with a twist: we apply DevOps practices to spacecraft control (we call it SatDevOps), and we'll train you to operate the satellites. What you'd own:
- Hybrid cloud infra on GCP + Kubernetes: provisioning (IaC), CI/CD, GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux)
- The observability stack (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, tracing) across ground and flight systems
- Reliability: RCAs, fault tolerance, performance tuning, long-term fixes over patches
- Software-defined networking between ground stations, cloud, and mission ops
- Developer experience: tooling and environments for the flight software and ops teams Looking for: strong public cloud (ideally GCP), deep Kubernetes, one backend language (Go/Python/Rust/C++/Java), IaC + CI/CD in anger, and someone who can design HA systems and then run them. Nice to have: FinOps, security tooling, orchestration in resource-constrained environments. Benefits: 100% company-paid medical/dental/vision for you and dependents, 401(k) + equity, flexible PTO + 12 holidays, 14/10 weeks paid parental leave, daily catered lunch, relocation assistance, and time with the team in France. Apply: https://jobs.lever.co/loftorbital/3ae5c3e3-c1e0-4311-83b5-0b... and mention HN in your application.

We build AI agents that look and sound human - real face, real voice, real-time conversation. The kind of thing that makes people ask if it's actually live the first time they see it. Looking for: 5+ years hands-on AWS in production, strong IaC, multi-cloud experience, low-latency systems, and startup experience. We're not able to offer relocation or visa sponsorship. title: AI Senior Engineer (Graph)
description:
Back in 2012, we were a group of engineers and designers who decided we wanted to build things—so we did. Able started as an engineering and product hub building for a portfolio of early-stage startups. We built many relationships while developing products that were thoughtful, effective, and genuinely useful. But, since then, we’ve grown… and so has our ambition. 

Now, we’re entering our next chapter—defined by applied AI. AI is a powerful force in the end-to-end software development cycle, and we’re creating practices that allow us to deliver software fast and more effectively than traditional approaches, creating meaningful value for our partners. Today, our builder mindset is driving us to become an AI-native organization across every function. We’re still evolving, and that’s part of the opportunity. If you want to build, learn, and tackle challenges alongside an ambitious team, let’s build together.

This position is 100% remote within LatAm. 

What you’ll be doing 

We are seeking someone who views the Knowledge Graph not just as a database, but as a living organism that requires constant care, feeding, and pruning. You understand that a RAG system is only as good as the data underlying it. You are intrigued by the complexity of ingesting massive, messy datasets and transforming them into clean, connected knowledge.

In short, someone who likes:

- Architecting Graph ETL: Designing and developing robust ETL pipelines specifically for graph ingestion. You aren't just dumping rows into tables; you are determining how disparate data sources connect, evolve, and relate in a graph structure.

- Data Ingestion at Scale: Managing high-volume data streams using tools like Kafka and implementing CDC (Change Data Capture) patterns to ensure the graph reflects real-time reality.

- Automated Graph Hygiene: Writing scripts and jobs for deduplication , orphan node detection , and data consistency checks. You take pride in a clean schema.

- Modeling Time: Handling complex temporal relationships (e.g., how property ownership or financial status changes over time) within the graph.

- Performance Tuning: Ensuring that as the graph grows (25k+ reports and beyond), the underlying query performance remains snappy through optimizing indexes and storage.

What we’re looking for 

We want to work with people who have a passion for collaborating with their teams, building software while nurturing inclusive and respectful relationships with their coworkers. With the ones that are open about their shortcomings and what they do not know now, but remain eager to keep on growing and closing those gaps.

Ideally, they would also have:

- Neo4j Expertise (Must Have): 4+ years of hands-on experience. You master Cypher , schema design, and the operational side of managing a production graph.

- ETL & Pipeline Mastery: Strong background in building data pipelines. You know how to take raw data, clean it, and structure it for graph ingestion.

- Streaming & CDC: Familiarity with event streaming platforms like Kafka and Change Data Capture methodologies to sync operational databases with the graph.

- Python Proficiency: Strong Python skills for writing ingestion scripts, maintenance jobs, and custom graph algorithms.

- Data Integrity Focus: Experience implementing automated jobs for entity resolution , deduplication, and quality assurance.

Nice-to-Have: 

- C# Knowledge: Ability to read or contribute to C# codebases.

- Domain Experience: Prior work in Finance or Real Estate sectors.

Able is powered by curious, thoughtful people who care about what they build and how they build it. We’re actively investing in our team through AI training, knowledge-sharing, and hands-on experimentation to ensure everyone grows alongside the technology.

This position is 100% remote within LatAm. Strong verbal and written communication skills in English are a requirement. As a team member, you can expect:

- To work 40 hours per week, and be available during normal business hours as needed.

- Payments made in USD.

- 18 days of PTO per year, observance of local holidays, and an annual break between Christmas and New Years.

- Wellness + Remote Stipend

- AI Voucher

About Able 

Able builds technology products in a portfolio model. We believe that people, teams, and processes are more important than the ideas themselves, so we’ve focused on bringing great people together, and investing in their growth.

We’ve built products in a variety of industries. Everything from media to finance to toys to healthcare. Sometimes we work with management teams to help their businesses grow faster or unlock value using technology. Other times we start or buy businesses outright. Each time, we look for opportunities to leverage technology built at the portfolio-level to drive value faster.

Able is committed to inclusion and diversity and is an equal-opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

This is but the beginning of a conversation we’d love to have with you.

Apply, and let’s get this adventure started!

title: Lumen Labs | Robotics / Hardware Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $130k–200k + equity | https://lumenresearch.co I'm Daniel, co-founder. Lumen Labs is building t
description: Lumen Labs | Robotics / Hardware Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $130k–200k + equity | https://lumenresearch.co I'm Daniel, co-founder. Lumen Labs is building the cognitive layer for physical AI. Nearly every major robotics effort today teaches machines by showing them thousands of hours of human teleoperation. We think that paradigm has a ceiling, and we're working on nature-inspired architectures for unstructured environments (construction sites, mining, pipelines, battlefield). Pre-seed, backed by top VC funds and operators from robotics/AI companies. We're a team of two and hiring teammate #3 to own the hardware and infrastructure that keeps our research platforms running: the ROS2 (Humble) stack across onboard and offboard compute, sensor integration and calibration (LiDAR, depth, IMU, encoders), the safety pipeline during autonomous runs, and getting trained policies onto real hardware. Today that's wheeled navigation; we're dipping our toes into drones and eyeing weirder platforms like pipeline inspection. Where we're at: zero-shot sim2real transfer with a policy that runs at 100Hz on an ESP32 and took under a day to train. You: hands-on with real mobile robots (UART, encoders, PWM, IMU, LiDAR), strong Python + embedded, comfortable reading code you didn't write, and can debug hardware and firmware at the same time. If "full-stack" to you means firmware, a multimeter, and a ROS node in the same afternoon, you'll fit right in. Visa/relocation support for the right person. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Robotics-Engineer-Ro... Email hi@lumenresearch.co, mention HN, and tell us about a project you've built. If you can link to a time you got a trained policy running on real hardware, you go to the top of the pile.

title: MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time
description:
MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time
MixRank processes petabytes of data every month through web crawling. Hundreds of customers use our data products, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries such as finance, recruiting, sales, marketing, and security. We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they genuinely love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs. Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests.
Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents. Junior Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more. To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build. Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/Fnwsojk-j Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re hiring generalist software engineers to work on web applications, data mining, machine learning/data science, data transformation/ETL, data modeling, database scaling, infrastructure, DevOps, and more. We’ll tailor the role to the subset of areas that best match your interests. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mixrank/jobs/RXQspen-s I’m Kiran, Chief of Staff at MixRank, a fully remote data startup building go-to-market intelligence. We’re US-incorporated but hire globally, and we’re bringing on new teammates to join a fast-moving team with real ownership and impact.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Canvas Core
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Canvas Core team builds and maintains the foundational platform that powers Mural ’s visual thinking experience. This includes the infinite canvas, key editor components, document editing behaviors, asset management, real-time collaboration, and the systems that enable fast, reliable, and intuitive interaction on the canvas.

We’re also responsible for the Mural UI, the real-time message protocol that enables seamless remote collaboration, and the developer-friendly APIs that internal teams use to build features like diagramming, workshops, presentations, integrations, and AI-enabled product capabilities.

Our mission is to ensure the Mural editor is fast, reliable, intuitive, and easy to build on.

We prioritize performance, simplicity, developer experience, and platform quality, enabling teams across the company to ship quickly and safely on top of Canvas Core.

YOUR MISSION

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll help design, build, and improve the Canvas platform so that the Mural editor remains reliable, high-performing, and intuitive for our users.

You’ll work on the systems that power real-time collaboration, shared document editing, spatial interactions, rendering and interaction performance, asset management, developer APIs, and AI-enabled product capabilities across the Mural editor.

Your role will be to reduce platform complexity, improve the quality and speed of Canvas development, and help teams ship high-quality editor experiences quickly and safely. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Engineering, and other stakeholders to turn ambiguous product and platform problems into clear, maintainable technical solutions.

Senior Engineers at Mural lead by example through strong technical execution, thoughtful design, high-quality implementation, and collaborative problem-solving. They help raise the bar for their team through design discussions, code reviews, mentoring, documentation, and pragmatic improvements to engineering practices.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- 
Own and deliver new Canvas platform capabilities and improvements from problem definition through implementation, release, measurement, and iteration

- 
Partner with Product and Design to shape high-quality user experiences, balancing pragmatic technical delivery with long-term platform needs

- 
Design and build maintainable Canvas platform systems, with accountability for quality, performance, reliability, and developer experience

- 
Contribute to developer-friendly APIs, service boundaries, and platform contracts that internal teams can build on quickly and safely

- 
Use AI-assisted tools and agentic workflows as part of your engineering practice to prototype, implement, test, document, and measure work effectively

- 
Strengthen the team through technical design reviews, demos, code reviews, mentoring, and improvements to engineering practices

-

Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the Role 

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

What You'll Do

- Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with the Integrations team, Case Strategy team, and other engineering and product partners to ensure systems are well-connected and aligned with how the broader platform operates.

- Contribute to front-end and admin workflows where needed: The role is primarily backend-focused, but you'll contribute to internal-facing UI and ops tooling where the product requires it.

- 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

- Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

- Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

- Comfortable operating in a collaborative, fast-moving startup environment where ownership and requirements evolve

- Python experience; able to work effectively in a Python-based backend environment

- Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

- Strong communicator who collaborates well across engineering, product, and adjacent teams

Extra Credit If You Have 

- Experience with healthcare-specific data or HealthTech systems

- Exposure to data-heavy architectures or problems adjacent to data engineering without being a pure data engineer

- Familiarity with tools like Snowflake, dbt, or Databricks

title: Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | Technical PM, ML Infra, Research Scientist/Engineer, Backend, Full Stack We build foundation models for tabular data. Deep
description: Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | Technical PM, ML Infra, Research Scientist/Engineer, Backend, Full Stack We build foundation models for tabular data. Deep learning transformed text and images but mostly skipped tables, which are still the data behind most clinical trials, financial models and scientific experiments. The reason is structural: no natural sequence, no spatial structure, no shared vocabulary across datasets, so the architectures and scaling laws behind LLMs don't transfer. Our approach: pre-train a transformer on millions of synthetic datasets sampled from causal-structure priors. The whole dataset goes in as context, predictions come out in one forward pass. No per-dataset training, no hyperparameter tuning, seconds instead of hours. TabPFN v2 was published in Nature and set a new state of the art; TabPFN-3 scales to 10M rows. 4M+ downloads, 8k+ GitHub stars, in production from liquid biopsy to rail maintenance. Code: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP, with more than EUR 1B committed over four years. Models stay open, research stays public, same team and offices. Roles (most can sit in any of the three offices): - Technical Product Manager, Integrations: take every model release live across SAP (AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud), the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, and help decide which channels we build next. Reports to me, close to the code. - ML Engineer, Infrastructure: own multi-cluster GPU infra (Slurm on GCP today, multi-provider next), training performance and the tooling layer. We spend tens of millions per year on compute; you own that budget. - Research Scientist, Foundation Model: drive the model agenda - novel architectures, scaling from 10K to 1M+ samples, multimodal and causal directions. PhD plus top-venue publications, or equivalent. - Research Engineer, Foundation Model: same agenda from the engineering side. You design experiments, write the training and eval infra, and co-author the papers. - ML Engineer, Backend: design and scale the backend that serves and finetunes the models. Python/FastAPI, Terraform, K8s. - Full Stack Engineer, ML Platform: build the product end to end. TypeScript + Python, React/FastAPI/Postgres. Also hiring: Applied Scientist, Forward Deployed ML Engineer, Research Scientist (Foundational Data Science), PhD research interns, plus GTM and ops roles. 40+ people with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Jane Street, Goldman, G-Research, CERN. Led by Frank Hutter, advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Yann LeCun. Comp competitive with top AI labs. All roles and applications: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/prior-labs Questions welcome in the replies here.

Store owners upload content, build playlists, pair outdoor Android screens from a phone, and see what is playing. The app is a mobile-first PWA. The screen on the sidewalk has its own states: setup QR, downloading, no content, and error. You take a real part in that breakdown. Bring a point of view on structure, priority, and what to cut. Versatility that spans the entire spectrum of data engineering in one or more of the following areas:

We structure problems and use the 80/20 rule(for many outcomes, roughly 80% of consequences come from 20% of causes) to identify where to direct our razor-sharp focus.

Each of us is passionate about excellence and growth, and we're encouraged to challenge the status quo and experiment with new methods. This mindset creates an environment where innovation is part of our daily routine and every team member is an impact-oriented trailblazer.

- 
By celebrating our successes and learning from our setbacks, we stay agile and forward-thinking, always striving to elevate our performance and impact.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

The team received a request from customers to show the running balance for assets tied to an address within the product. They successfully delivered the feature on schedule, impressing customers with both the functionality and the speed of execution.

- 
The team was tasked with developing a solution to reveal Indirect Exposure through cross-chain swaps in response to a competitor's similar feature. With this input, the team devised a solution that fit the timeline, communicated the tradeoffs to stakeholders, and successfully delivered the solution as promised.

fractile.ai - AI hardware, backed by Founders Fund - London (UK) - Onsite ABOUT FRACTILE
Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the amount of time they take to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. We’ve recently raised $220M from Founders Fund and Accel and the most important work lies ahead. Come and join the mission! THE ROLE
As a Software Engineer you will be a core part of our technical team working alongside the hardware, software and research teams to solve cutting-edge problems in AI hardware, ranging from verification to simulation, alongside the best of the best (DeepMind, Apple, Meta…). ABOUT YOU

It’s likely you have several years of professional experience, but we will make exceptions for the right candidate 4. You want to work with the best. And you are excited to work in chips, solving the hardest problems at the frontier of AI WHAT WE OFFER
1. Competitive compensation and meaningful equity
2. A very cool office with London's best views
3. Private medical insurance and pension benefits If this sounds like you, ping carmen@fractile.ai
